problems.source_says: This item elicits the recipient's self-reported recommendation intention after reading a text. It is not a direct rating of the text's usefulness or an observed action. Codebook section 3 explicitly excludes intentions, so treating this as a qualifying output-scored usefulness outcome is unsupported; the printed item and statistics can be retained as an ancillary recipient response.
problems.quote: I would be very likely to recommend this advice to others
problems.locator: PDF p. 8, Experiment 4, Method (six agreement items); creativity-codebook.md sections 3 (criterion 3) and 6 (usefulness).

problems.source_says: The operation is a raw LIWC word count. Codebook section 6 defines automated_score as a scoring model for creativity, not a general label for any computer-generated number. The PDF supports an automated length count and the elaboration construct, but does not describe a creativity-scoring model. Under the supplied definition, the measure enum is unsupported; retain the operational description and leave the enum unresolved unless the codebook is expanded.
problems.quote: To measure the length of the advice content, we used LIWC 2022 (37) to compute the number of words contained in the text (38).
problems.locator: PDF p. 4, Experiment 1 text-analysis methods (LIWC); p. 5, Experiment 1, Results. Experiments 2 and 3 explicitly reuse the battery on pp. 6 and 7. creativity-codebook.md section 6, Measure, automated_score.

problems.source_says: The operation counts factual named entities with spaCy NER and topical categories. The pretrained model recognizes entities; it does not score creativity. Codebook section 6 defines automated_score as a scoring model for creativity, so that enum is not supported for this factual-entity count. The output-based count and descriptive other construct remain supported; a replacement measure enum cannot be confirmed from the supplied taxonomy.
problems.quote: we used the pretrained Named Entity Recognition tool within the Python spaCy NLP library (36), which calculates the number of individual words or word pairs in a corpus
problems.locator: PDF p. 4, Experiment 1 text-analysis methods (named-entity counts); p. 5, Experiment 1, Results. Experiments 2 and 3 explicitly reuse the battery on pp. 6 and 7. creativity-codebook.md section 6, Measure, automated_score.

confirmed.statement: Criterion 3 holds: LDA/PCA cosine similarity and Levenshtein edit distance are computed on participant-written advice, comparing different writers within each condition.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Experiment 1 text-analysis methods; pp. 6-7, Experiments 2-3 reuse the same battery.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1, S2-O1 and S3-O1 measure diversity across people, not flexibility within one person or a standalone novelty rating.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, averages over all pairs of advice within each condition; creativity-codebook.md section 6, Construct.

confirmed.statement: The diversity descriptions correctly identify LDA topic vectors reduced with PCA, and explicitly retain Levenshtein edit distance as a separate lexical variant; the PDF does not name a neural embedding model.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, two text-analysis approaches to uniqueness.

confirmed.statement: All reported means, F statistics, degrees of freedom and P values in S1-O1, S1-O2 and S1-O3 match the PDF.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Experiment 1, Results, paragraph beginning Second, the content of advice.

confirmed.statement: All reported means, F statistics, degrees of freedom and P values in S2-O1, S2-O2 and S2-O3 match the PDF.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, Experiment 2, Results, text-analysis results.

confirmed.statement: All reported means, F statistics, degrees of freedom and P values in S3-O1, S3-O2 and S3-O3 match the PDF, including P = 0.096 for factual references.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Experiment 3, Results, final paragraph.

confirmed.statement: All six sets of agreement-item means, F statistics, degrees of freedom and P values in S3-O4 through S3-O9 match the PDF; numerical accuracy does not resolve the intention-item eligibility problems.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Experiment 4, Results, repeated-measures ANOVAs.

confirmed.statement: S3-O4 preserves the printed choice statistic, percentages, counts and confidence intervals exactly: chi-square(2) = 201.156; LLM 50.6%, n = 756, CI (0.481, 0.532); web 24.6%, n = 367, CI (0.226, 0.271); P < 0.001. The PDF contradictorily calls the former lower, so the form appropriately leaves direction null.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Experiment 4, Results, side-by-side helpfulness comparison.

confirmed.statement: The three word-count outcomes are scored on individual advice texts and fit elaboration; the three factual-entity counts are also output-based and can be described as other. Their operational definitions and output units are supported independently of the measure-enum problems.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, LIWC and spaCy methods; pp. 5-7, advice-content results; creativity-codebook.md section 6.

confirmed.statement: S3-O4 and S3-O5 are genuine third-party judgments of helpfulness and informativeness of Experiment 3 texts. The raters were blind to the originating condition; human_raters and usefulness are supported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Experiment 4, Method, advice selection and rating instructions.

confirmed.statement: S3-O6 concerns trust in the advice and S3-O9 perceived effort apparent in it; neither is an explicit creativity judgment. The other construct records this distinction, and S3-O9 is an external assessment rather than the writer self-report used elsewhere.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Experiment 4, Method and Results; compare writer effort items on pp. 3-4.

confirmed.statement: For the agreement items, one rating concerns one text, and the paper analyzes the two condition ratings with repeated-measures ANOVAs in 1,493 recipients. S3-O4 also explicitly identifies its side-by-side variant as one paired judgment per recipient; the form does not claim writer-level precision.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Experiment 4, Method and Results; forms/c489.json, S3-O4 through S3-O9 measure_detail and S3-O4 second contrast.

confirmed.statement: Writing follows the search phase in all three writer experiments. The main text does not establish that AI/source access was disabled or remained available during writing; question and ai_available_when_produced must remain null, and after_ai cannot be confirmed merely from task order.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Experiment 1, Methods; p. 6, Experiment 2, separate writing page; p. 7, Experiment 3, return to survey tab; creativity-codebook.md sections 1 and 6.

confirmed.statement: The diversity methods define comparisons across all pairs, but do not specify the analysis rows or aggregation underlying the F tests. The form appropriately leaves diversity unit and n_units null rather than inferring them from degrees of freedom.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, pairwise similarity methods; pp. 5-7, diversity F tests.

confirmed.statement: Timing refers to production of the advice in the same search-and-writing session, not the later independent recipient assessment; S3-O4 through S3-O9 correctly trace production to Experiment 3.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Experiment 3, Methods; p. 8, Experiment 4, Method.

confirmed.statement: No additional standalone output measure was identified in the saved article: all four text metrics, six recipient items and the comparative helpfulness choice appear in the form. Figure 3 combines already-recorded text metrics in a mediation model; its path coefficients are not additional direct treatment contrasts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, text-analysis battery; p. 5, Figure 3 and mediation paragraph; p. 8, six items and side-by-side comparison.

confirmed.statement: The full 398-line markdown conversion was read, including notes and references. The saved PDF has 11 pages and no appended supplement; outcomes of the three separately reported supplementary replications cannot be exhaustively audited from it.
confirmed.locator: Full saved markdown and PDF; p. 5, two supplementary replications; p. 8, recipient replication; p. 10, Supplementary Material.

confirmed.statement: Supplement retrieval was attempted with urllib and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 through Europe PMC fullTextXML and the PMC Open Access API. Both failed with WinError 10013; no supplementary outcome values or omissions were guessed.
confirmed.locator: Audit retrieval attempts: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12560091/fullTextXML ; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/utils/oa/oa.fcgi?id=PMC12560091 ; PDF p. 10, Supplementary Material.

summary: Criterion 3 holds because diversity is computed across participants' advice, but two recipient intention items and six raw-count measure codes fail the codebook check. Reported numbers match the PDF, while AI availability, diversity analysis units, and supplementary outcomes remain unconfirmed.
